bed bugs fed 21 d before testing are the most tolerant of deltamethin, followed by bed bugs fed 9 d before testing, and finally, bed bugs fed 3 d before testing.
the effects of starvation on insecticide tolerance in bed bugs are complex and depend on the time since feeding and the method of toxicity assessment.
starvation for 21 d results in a significant decrease in tolerance to deltamethrin, while starvation for 2 d has no effect on tolerance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
21 d of starvation increases tolerance to deltamethrin in bed bugs, and this is likely a result of a physiological change that occurs following feeding.

9 d starvated adult male bed bugs were most sensitive to the pyrethroid deltamethrin, and 2 d starvated bugs had the least sensitive, and that the difference between the two was due to the mass of the bug and not the amount of blood meal consumed.
9 d is the best time point to test deltamethrin toxicity to bed bugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bed bugs that are 2 d or less starved have the same tolerance as bed bugs that are fed, and therefore, insecticide bioassay results from starved bugs can be extrapolated to fed bugs.
bed bug control efforts will be more effective if bed bugs are not starved before treatment.
bed bugs that are starved for 21 d are much more susceptible to deltamethrin than those starved for 9 d, which is important information for pest management professionals and homeowners.
